title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Company Person
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management, persons who work closely with Senior Management and/or work in the finance or strategy team, IT staff who may have access to sensitive materials, other employees who may possess market sensitive information before the market, and any other person designated a Company Person by the Board in writing. Subject to the whole policy: insider trading, Blackout Periods, protection arrangements (section 5.2), and the security/margin lending restriction (section 5.3).

definitions.hedging_definition: Operate to limit the economic risk of any Company Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including the Company's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under any Company incentive plan) on that Company Person's behalf

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Any other period that the Board specifies from time to time is also a mandated Blackout Period. The Policy does not state whether such a period is disclosed or kept confidential.

rules.detail: 'Protection arrangements' expressly extend to 'Company products in the derivatives markets'. Entering into any such arrangement over unvested securities is prohibited at any time, with no consent route.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of 'protection arrangements' for any Company securities (or Company products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: The same outright ban extends to securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Once vested and unlocked, a protection arrangement (including a derivative such as an OTC put/call) is permitted with prior consent from the applicable Authorising Officer under paragraph 4.2, confirming no Inside Information.
Hedging arrangements are expressly named as an example of a 'protection arrangement' that operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding; banned outright over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: Operate to limit the economic risk of any Company Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including the Company's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under any Company incentive plan) on that Company Person's behalf;

rules.detail: The same outright hedging ban extends to vested securities subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Hedging vested, unlocked securities is permitted with prior consent from the Authorising Officer under 4.2.
Monetisation is not named. A structure such as a prepaid forward operates to limit the economic risk of a holding and so is a 'protection arrangement'; banned outright over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: Operate to limit the economic risk of any Company Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including the Company's securities held beneficially ... on that Company Person's behalf;

rules.detail: Once vested and unlocked, a monetisation structure is a permitted protection arrangement with prior consent under 4.2.

Short selling beyond the Company Person's holding is expressly a 'protection arrangement'; as it involves securities the person does not hold, it falls within the outright, no-consent prohibition rather than the consent-based route.
rules.evidence: Amount to 'short selling' of securities beyond the Company Person's holding of securities;

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are expressly named as an example of a derivative-market transaction banned outright only if short term or speculative (5.1); a CFD that limits the economic risk of a holding is also a 'protection arrangement' under 5.2, banned outright if unvested/locked, else requiring consent under 4.2.
rules.evidence: transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Outright ban on entering a margin lending arrangement involving unvested or holding-locked Company securities, with no consent route.
rules.evidence: Company Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Company Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities.

rules.detail: The same outright ban extends to vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Once vested and unlocked, entering a margin lending arrangement is permitted with prior consent under 4.2.
rules.evidence: Unless paragraph (a) applies, Company Persons may, directly or indirectly, ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities, with consent under paragraph 4.2.

rules.detail: Outright ban on granting any form of security (charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over unvested or holding-locked Company securities, to secure any obligation of the Company Person or a third party.

rules.detail: The security/margin lending ban is drafted broadly to cover 'any form of security ... to secure any obligation of that Company Person or any third party' -- not limited to margin loans -- and applies to any secured financing over unvested or holding-locked securities, with no consent route.

rules.detail: Once vested and unlocked, any secured financing arrangement (not limited to margin loans) secured on the Company securities is permitted with prior consent under 4.2 -- this is the provision that governs a bank loan secured on collared shares.
rules.evidence: Unless paragraph (a) applies, Company Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company securities, to secure any obligation of that Company Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities, with consent under paragraph 4.2.

rules.detail: Ban on short-term or speculative trading in Company securities, including short-term direct dealing and derivative-market transactions (exchange-traded options, share warrants, CFDs and similar instruments); no fixed holding period is specified.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Company Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Company securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

exceptions.evidence: trade Company securities where the trading does not result in a change of beneficial interest in the securities;

acquire securities under any director or employee security plan or through the exercise of options or performance rights under an option or performance rights plan or acquire, or agree to acquire, options or performance rights under an option or performance rights plan.
transfer Company securities already held into a self-managed superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary;
acquire the Company's ordinary shares by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to the Company's ordinary shares;
acquire the Company's securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class;
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer;

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;
a disposal of Company securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement;

where a restricted person is a trustee, trade in the securities managed by that trust provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person;

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

financing_disclosure: Company Person; trigger: entering a security or margin lending arrangement, or a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement (s6(a)(viii)); to: the relevant Authorising Officer; deadline: not specified (s6(b))

exemption_authority: The Board has absolute discretion to determine 'exceptional circumstances' case-by-case (s4.3(b)), which may include severe financial hardship or a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking; the Authorising Officer may then approve dealing during a Blackout Period, or other dealing otherwise prohibited by the Policy (s4.3(a)), with approval given by email and the standing notification requirements still applying. There is no exemption route for the outright bans on unvested or holding-locked securities in sections 5.2(a) and 5.3(a), which apply 'at any time'.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Company Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The secured-financing ban applies only to unvested or holding-locked shares; once vested and unlocked, granting security over the shares to secure a bank loan is expressly permitted with prior consent, so the loan leg of a funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares is achievable.

bespoke_clauses.topic: broad scope of secured financing ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company securities ... to secure any obligation of that Company Person or any third party
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban (and its consent-based release once vested) is not limited to margin loans -- it covers any secured financing including a bilateral bank loan -- so the bank's collar loan is squarely regulated by, and can rely on, section 5.3 rather than sitting in a gap.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares is exempt from the Blackout Period and consent requirements, though the Company Person must still notify the Authorising Officer after the event.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Company Person seeking authorisation cannot be their own Authorising Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirms a layered approval chain (e.g. the Board Chair is cleared by the Audit & Risk Committee Chair) that cannot be bypassed by self-approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: after dealing with Company securities, provide the Authorising Officer with a transaction confirmation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into, and settlement or unwind of, the collar and loan must be reported to the Authorising Officer, though no specific deadline is stated.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under Pepper Money's policy once the shares have vested and are no longer subject to a holding lock, subject to prior consent. Both the derivative legs (protection arrangements, including hedging and limiting economic risk) under section 5.2, and the secured-financing leg (granting any form of security to secure any obligation of the Company Person or a third party, or a margin lending arrangement) under section 5.3, are banned outright with no consent route only while the shares are unvested or holding-locked; once vested and unlocked, both are expressly permitted with prior written consent from the applicable Authorising Officer (the Audit and Risk Committee Chair for the Board Chair, the Board Chair for other directors/KMP/Company Secretary, and the CEO for everyone else), confirming no Inside Information and outside a Blackout Period unless the Board grants an exceptional-circumstances waiver for hardship or legal compulsion. The secured-financing prohibition is drafted broadly and is not limited to margin loans, so the bank's collar loan is squarely covered by, and released by, the same vesting-gated consent regime as the derivative legs. A secured lender's enforcement sale of the collared shares is exempted from the Blackout Period and consent requirements, though it must still be notified to the Authorising Officer afterwards. Overall, provided the collar and loan are entered into over vested, unlocked shares with prior consent and outside a Blackout Period, the structure appears permitted.
